Savior Plumbing Inc. — Phone Intake & Dispatch Guide — Internal Use Only Page 1
SAVIOR PLUMBING INC.Serving Alameda & Contra Costa Counties • (925) 232-8896 • saviorplumbing.com
PHONE INTAKE & DISPATCH GUIDE
For office staff and anyone answering the main line. Revision 9 — February 2026. Keep this at the desk.
The single most important rule: we would rather take four extra minutes on the phone than roll a truck to the wrong job. Get the address, the problem, and whether water is actively running. Everything else can be sorted out later.
1. Answering the Call
Answer within three rings. Standard greeting:
“Thank you for calling Savior Plumbing, this is ______. How can I help you today?”
If the caller opens in Spanish, switch or transfer. We are a bilingual shop and this is a point of pride — never make a Spanish-speaking caller struggle through English.
Set the frame early
• Get the caller's name in the first 30 seconds and use it through the call.
• Let them describe the problem once, uninterrupted, before you start asking questions.
• Confirm you understand by playing it back: “So the water heater is leaking from the bottom and there's water on the garage floor — is that right?”
• Never dead-air. If you're typing, say you're typing.
2. Required Intake Fields
Every call, without exception. A job cannot be dispatched without the first six.
# Field Notes / how to ask
1 Caller name First and last. Spell the last name back.
2 Best callback number Confirm whether it accepts text — techs text their ETA.
3 Service address Full street address plus city. Gate or unit number if applicable.
4 Property type House, condo, apartment, or commercial. Changes who we send.
5 Owner or tenant If tenant, we need landlord or property manager authorization before work.
6 Problem description In the customer's own words first, then your triage questions.
7 How long has it been happening
Distinguishes emergency from routine.
8 Is water actively running or leaking now
This is the emergency trigger. Ask it on every water call.
9 Have they shut off the water
If not, walk them through it — see section 4.

Savior Plumbing Inc. — Phone Intake & Dispatch Guide — Internal Use Only Page 2
# Field Notes / how to ask
10 Has anyone else worked on it
Recent work by others changes our approach and our warranty.
11 Access constraints Dogs, gate codes, stairs, parking, hours the building allows work.
12 Preferred appointment window
Offer what dispatch actually has. Do not invent availability.
13 How they heard about us Google, Yelp, referral, repeat customer, drove by.
3. Triage Matrix
Use this to decide urgency. When in doubt, treat it as more urgent, not less.
Caller says Priority What to do
Water actively flooding, cannot stop it
EMERGENC
Y
Walk them to the main shutoff immediately (section 4). Then get dispatch on it. Interrupt Danny if needed.
Sewage backing up into the home
EMERGENC
Y
Health hazard. Tell them to stop using all water fixtures. Same-day if at all possible.
Smell of gas EMERGENC
Y
Stop. Tell them to leave the building and call PG&E at 1-800-743-5000
first. We come after the utility clears it.
No water at all in the house Urgent Same-day if we have capacity. Ask if neighbors also lost water — may be a utility issue, not us.
No hot water Urgent Same-day if possible. Get the water heater's age, fuel type, and location before dispatch.
Water heater leaking Urgent Ask if it's dripping or pouring. Pouring from the tank body means replacement, not repair.
Only toilet in the home is clogged
Urgent Treat as urgent. If they have a second working bathroom, it drops to same-week.
Slow drain, one fixture Routine Next available. Usually 1–3 business days.
Dripping faucet, running toilet Routine Next available. Bundle with other small items if they have any.
Wants a quote for a remodel or repipe
Estimate visit Book a site visit. Written quote follows by next business day.
Commercial property, any issue
Route to
Danny
Do not quote. Take full details and have Danny call back.
4. Talking a Caller Through the Main Shutoff
You are not giving plumbing advice. You are stopping property damage while we drive there. Stay calm and keep your voice slow.
“Okay, I want to get the water stopped first and then we'll talk about getting someone out. Are you able to walk outside for me?”
• Most homes here: the shutoff is in a concrete box at the street near the sidewalk, or on an exterior wall near the front hose bibb.
• Turn direction: clockwise, or turn the lever so it sits crosswise to the pipe.

Savior Plumbing Inc. — Phone Intake & Dispatch Guide — Internal Use Only Page 3
• Water heater only: there is usually a separate valve on the cold inlet on top of the heater.
• If they can't find it or can't turn it: stop. Don't have them force anything. Escalate to same-day dispatch and stay on the line if they're panicking.
Never instruct a caller to open a gas line, relight a pilot on a unit that smells of gas, or use a drain chemical. If a caller has already poured chemical drain cleaner down the line, note it on the work order — the tech needs to know before they open anything.
5. Scheduling Rules
Topic Rule
Business hours Monday–Friday, 7:30am to 4:30pm. Office closed Saturday and Sunday.
Weekends / after hours By appointment only. Do not book directly — take the details and tell them the office will confirm.
Appointment windows Two-hour windows. Morning 8–10, 10–12. Afternoon 12–2, 2–4.
Same-day Often available but never guaranteed. Say “often we can” — never “we will.”
ETA calls The tech calls or texts 20–30 minutes out. Tell the customer to expect this.
Running late If a tech will miss the window, the office calls the customer before the window closes. Not after.
Cancellations No fee if cancelled before the tech is dispatched.
Rescheduling Free. Just move it. Don't make the customer feel bad about it.
Service area Alameda and Contra Costa counties. If they're outside, say so honestly and offer a referral if you know one.
6. What You Can and Cannot Say About Price
You CAN say You CANNOT say
The diagnostic fee is $89 during business hours, and it's waived if they approve the repair that same visit.
A firm price for any repair before a tech has seen it.
Estimates are free for most services. An after-hours or weekend price. That rate is not finalized
— take a message.
Larger or complex projects get a written quote by the next business day.
Any commercial price. Route to Danny.
All our pricing is flat rate, so they'll know the full price before any work starts.
An hourly rate. We do not sell hours.
We honor a 2-year labor warranty on our work. That a specific past job is covered — check the history first.
A general range, clearly labeled as a range, for very common jobs (see the price book).
A range for anything you had to look up twice. If you're unsure, don't.
“I don't want to guess and be wrong — that's not how we do it. What I can tell you is the diagnostic is $89, and if you go ahead with the repair we take that off. The technician gives you the full flat-rate price before he touches anything.”

7. Common Questions and Approved Answers
Question Answer
Are you licensed and insured? Yes. Licensed, bonded, and insured. Our techs are trained journeyman plumbers.
How long have you been around? Since 2000. Family-owned and locally operated.
Do you have a warranty? Two-year labor warranty on our work.
Are you Diamond Certified? Yes — 14 consecutive years, and voted best in Pleasanton.
Do you speak Spanish? Yes, our team is bilingual.
Do you do commercial? Yes. Take details and route to Danny for the quote.
Can I pay online? Yes, there's a Pay Online page on our website.
What payment methods? NOT DOCUMENTED — confirm with Marisol before answering.
Do you offer financing? NOT DOCUMENTED — do not promise. Take a message.
Do you work with home warranty companies?
NOT DOCUMENTED — escalate to the office.
Do you bill insurance for water damage? NOT DOCUMENTED — escalate.
Is there a senior or military discount? NOT DOCUMENTED — escalate.
Can you give me a price over the phone? Explain flat-rate and the diagnostic. See section 6.
8. Escalation & Transfers
Route to For
Dispatch — ext. 101 Scheduling, changes, ETA questions, adding a job to the board.
Danny O. — ext. 103 Commercial anything, pricing questions, scope disputes, tech escalations.
Marisol R. — ext. 102 Billing, invoices, warranty verification, complaints, payment questions.
Owner Only if Marisol and Danny are both unavailable and the caller is escalating.
Handling an upset caller
• Let them finish. Do not defend, explain, or interrupt.
• Acknowledge the specific thing that went wrong, not a generic apology.
• Never blame the technician, the schedule, or another company while on the phone.
• Commit to one concrete next step with a time attached: “Marisol will call you back before 4 o'clock today.”
• Then actually make sure that happens. A missed callback is how a two-star review gets written.
9. Taking a Message
If nobody can take the call, the message must contain all of the following or it's not useful:
• Name, callback number, and whether the number takes texts.
• Service address.
• One-line problem summary in the caller's words.

Savior Plumbing Inc. — Phone Intake & Dispatch Guide — Internal Use Only Page 5
• Urgency per the triage matrix.
• What you told them — especially any timeframe you promised.
• Who it needs to go to and by when.
